## Setup

`evaluation_functions.R` loads the wrangled snapshots with the shared season
split attached, and provides the cross-validation and scoring tools every model
uses. Run `Data_Wrangling_LivePred.R` first if `Data/derived/live_analysis.rds`
does not exist.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(ranger)

source("evaluation_functions.R")
live <- load_model_data()
options(width = 120)  # print wide tables without truncating columns
```

What we are working with: one row per completed rally, with the season split
attached in `live$meta`.

```{r}
#| label: data-overview
dim(live$x_score)   # 4 score predictors
dim(live$x_skills)  # 4 score predictors + 38 cumulative skill counts
table(role = live$meta$role, fold = live$meta$fold, useNA = "ifany")
```

## Step 1: Baseline forest

A probability forest with default settings, fitted on two feature sets:

- `score`: the same four inputs as the score-only logistic baseline.
- `score_skills`: the score inputs plus the 38 cumulative skill counts.

Comparing the two tells us whether the forest can extract information from the
skill counts that the logistic model could not.

`case.weights` makes each set count equally, as in the baselines. We do not
use the forest's out-of-bag error: rallies from the same set are nearly
identical, so out-of-bag rows are not truly unseen.

```{r}
#| label: rf-functions
rf_fit <- function(x, y, w) {
  ranger(x = x, y = y, case.weights = w, probability = TRUE,
         num.trees = 500, seed = 4640)
}
rf_predict <- function(model, x) {
  predict(model, x)$predictions[, "win"]
}
```

Season cross-validation: each training season is predicted by a forest fitted
on the other three. The test seasons are not touched.

```{r}
#| label: rf-default-cv
rf_cv <- bind_rows(
  cv_predictions(live, live$x_score, rf_fit, rf_predict) |>
    mutate(model = "rf_default", feature_set = "score"),
  cv_predictions(live, live$x_skills, rf_fit, rf_predict) |>
    mutate(model = "rf_default", feature_set = "score_skills")
)
```

Compare with the baselines on the same cross-validation snapshots. Lower is
better; `diff_vs_ref` is the Brier difference from the score-only logistic
model (negative = better).

```{r}
#| label: rf-default-scores
baseline_cv <- read_predictions() |> filter(split == "cv")
step1 <- score_predictions(bind_rows(baseline_cv, rf_cv), live$meta)

step1$summary |>
  select(model, feature_set, brier, log_loss, diff_vs_ref, diff_low, diff_high)
```

Where in the set does each model do well or poorly?

```{r}
#| label: rf-default-stages
step1$by_stage |>
  mutate(model = paste(model, feature_set, sep = "__")) |>
  select(model, stage, brier) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = stage, values_from = brier)
```

## Step 2: Tuning

The default forest grows leaves down to 10 rallies. Rallies from the same set
share almost all of their inputs and the same outcome, so small leaves memorize
individual sets rather than learning patterns that carry over to new seasons.
We tune two settings:

- `min.node.size`: the smallest leaf the forest will split. Larger leaves
  average over more sets.
- `mtry`: how many predictors each split may choose from. Smaller values force
  the forest to use weaker predictors more often.

We also try a third feature set, `score_skilldiff`: the score inputs plus the
19 home-minus-away skill differences (e.g. CU kills minus opponent kills). It
keeps the skill information in a smaller set of predictors.

```{r}
#| label: skilldiff-features
home_cols <- grep("^home_", colnames(live$x_skills), value = TRUE)
x_skilldiff <- live$x_skills[, home_cols] -
  live$x_skills[, sub("^home_", "away_", home_cols)]
colnames(x_skilldiff) <- sub("^home_", "diff_", home_cols)
x_skilldiff <- cbind(live$x_score, x_skilldiff)

feature_sets <- list(score = live$x_score, score_skills = live$x_skills,
                     score_skilldiff = x_skilldiff)
```

Every combination is scored by season cross-validation. The grid uses 300 trees
to save time and the set-averaged Brier score without intervals.

```{r}
#| label: tuning-grid
rf_fit_with <- function(mtry, min_node, num_trees = 300) {
  function(x, y, w) {
    ranger(x = x, y = y, case.weights = w, probability = TRUE,
           num.trees = num_trees, mtry = mtry, min.node.size = min_node,
           seed = 4640)
  }
}

cv_scores <- function(pred) {
  add_losses(pred, live$meta) |>
    group_by(match_id, set_number) |>
    summarise(brier = mean(brier), log_loss = mean(log_loss), .groups = "drop") |>
    summarise(brier = mean(brier), log_loss = mean(log_loss))
}

grid <- bind_rows(
  expand_grid(feature_set = "score", mtry = 2:4,
              min_node = c(10, 100, 400, 800, 1200, 1600, 2400)),
  expand_grid(feature_set = "score_skills", mtry = c(6, 14, 28, 42),
              min_node = c(100, 400, 800, 1600, 2400)),
  expand_grid(feature_set = "score_skilldiff", mtry = c(4, 12, 23),
              min_node = c(400, 1600, 2400))
)

tuning <- grid |>
  mutate(scores = pmap(list(feature_set, mtry, min_node), function(fs, m, n) {
    cv_predictions(live, feature_sets[[fs]], rf_fit_with(m, n), rf_predict) |>
      cv_scores()
  })) |>
  unnest(scores)
```

Leaf size matters most. CV Brier score by leaf size, for the best `mtry` at
each size:

```{r}
#| label: tuning-leaf-size
tuning |>
  group_by(feature_set, min_node) |>
  summarise(brier = min(brier), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(min_node, brier, colour = feature_set)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.158, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Minimum leaf size (rallies, log scale)", y = "CV Brier score",
       colour = "Features",
       caption = "Dashed line: score-only logistic baseline") +
  theme_minimal()
```

The best settings for each feature set:

```{r}
#| label: tuning-best
best <- tuning |>
  group_by(feature_set) |>
  slice_min(brier, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()
best
```

These scores are slightly optimistic, because the settings were chosen on the
same cross-validation folds they are scored on.

## Step 3: Tuned forests

Refit the best settings for each feature set with 500 trees and compare with
the baselines, with intervals.

```{r}
#| label: rf-tuned-cv
rf_tuned_cv <- best |>
  pmap(function(feature_set, mtry, min_node, ...) {
    cv_predictions(live, feature_sets[[feature_set]],
                   rf_fit_with(mtry, min_node, num_trees = 500), rf_predict) |>
      mutate(model = "random_forest", feature_set = feature_set)
  }) |>
  bind_rows()

step3 <- score_predictions(bind_rows(baseline_cv, rf_tuned_cv), live$meta)
step3$summary |>
  select(model, feature_set, brier, log_loss, diff_vs_ref, diff_low, diff_high)
```

```{r}
#| label: rf-tuned-stages
step3$by_stage |>
  mutate(model = paste(model, feature_set, sep = "__")) |>
  select(model, stage, brier) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = stage, values_from = brier)
```

Which predictors does the tuned skills forest split on? Impurity importance
measures how much each predictor reduces error across the forest's splits; it
is a description of the fitted model, not a test.

```{r}
#| label: rf-importance
skills_best <- filter(best, feature_set == "score_skills")
train_rows <- live$meta$role == "train"
importance_fit <- ranger(
  x = live$x_skills[train_rows, ], y = live$y[train_rows],
  case.weights = live$meta$set_weight[train_rows], probability = TRUE,
  num.trees = 500, mtry = skills_best$mtry,
  min.node.size = skills_best$min_node, importance = "impurity", seed = 4640
)
enframe(importance_fit$variable.importance, "predictor", "importance") |>
  mutate(share = importance / sum(importance)) |>
  arrange(desc(importance)) |>
  head(10)
```

## Step 4: Save predictions

Save the tuned forests in the standard format so `compare_models.R` includes
them. `run_model()` also fits on all training seasons and predicts the test
seasons; those predictions are saved but not examined here.

```{r}
#| label: rf-save
best |>
  pwalk(function(feature_set, mtry, min_node, ...) {
    run_model(live, feature_sets[[feature_set]],
              rf_fit_with(mtry, min_node, num_trees = 500), rf_predict) |>
      save_predictions(model = "random_forest", feature_set = feature_set)
  })
```
